title: Which token does the circuit copy?

doesNotKnow: Sequence A B X A. At the final A, match keys equal to the previous token of each historical value. What is copied?

objective: Compute this finite induction-heads model, compare earned countercases, and explain its stated boundary.

claims.text:
induction-heads

**Identity / target / source:** `ai:induction-heads` → `ai-induction-heads` → `src/demos/ai/ai-induction-heads`; source `company/domains/proposals/2026-10-18-ai-map-expansion.json#concepts/159`; brief `company/domains/briefs/2026-10-19-ai-next30e.md#28-induction-heads`. **Packet:** I2. **Level / prerequisites:** stretch; `ai:attention-weights`, `ai:in-context-learning`.

**Nearest / distinct payoff:** attention-weights combines values by weights; this computes an explicit shifted-key match-and-copy circuit on a repeated token pattern.

**Computed primary model:** Sequence[A,B,X,A], final queryA. A previous-token stage creates at historical value positionj≥1 the keytoken[j−1] and valuetoken[j]. A hard one-hot match stage selects the latest historicalj<finalposition whose key equals current query. Atj1 keyA/valueB, so circuit predictsB. It is not direct copying of the earlierA token itself.

**Countercase / boundary:** Change sequence[A,C,X,A]: matched value becomesC. Sequence[A,B,X,Y] has no matching historical keyY and yieldsUnknown. Conflicting successors[A,B,A,C,A] choose latestC under explicit tie rule. This supplied causal circuit is an induction-head analogue, not learned softmax attention or an explanation of every form of in-context learning.

**Prediction / transfer recall:** Predict copied token from original shifted key/value table; recall why a broken match must not hallucinate a learned successor and why the fixed recency rule matters.

**Intervention / retained witness:** Build shifted keys then Match/copy computes attention selection and copied token; Change successor/No match/Conflicting matches expose the exact boundaries with originalB retained. Show both causal stages and historical indices, not an answer string toggle.

**Source obligation:** [Olsson et al. original PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2209.11895), opened2026-10-19, induction pattern [A][B]…[A]→[B] and two-head mechanism discussion. The hard shifted-key circuit and tie rule are local declared simplifications; no pretrained-head or broad ICL causal claim.
